title: Edge Flushback and Inflight Priority Protocol — Sketch
content:
Context:
This is a lightweight personal sketch for an experiment: attach a client-visible backpressure / flushback signal and an inflight-priority header so edge proxies can make smarter decisions about prewarm, flush frequency and which requests to admit during congestion. Goal is a pragmatic, minimal API shape that can be implemented in client SDKs + edge proxy with incremental rollouts.

Problem we want to solve:
- Clients (mobile/web) generate lots of short conversational interactions with mixed importance: interactive typing updates (low priority), user-submitted prompts (high priority), background prefetches (low/medium).
- Under congestion or when KV-cache misses happen, we need a way to: 1) throttle low-value requests earlier, 2) flush partial responses back to client as cheaply as possible, 3) maintain telemetry to diagnose which request classes get degraded.

Design principles (tradeoffs):
- Keep change surface small for clients: a header or small JSON envelope on existing REST/HTTP/GRPC calls. No new long-lived connections required.
- Edge proxy should be able to make per-tenant decisions using simple counters and token-bucket style admission.
- Telemetry labels required for postmortem and SLO accounting.
- Graceful fallback: if header absent, preserve current behavior.

API shape (proposal):
1) Outgoing request headers (client -> edge):
   - X-RW-Priority: string enum ("critical" | "interactive" | "background" | "prefetch")
   - X-RW-Soft-Timeout-ms: integer (how long client is willing to wait; not a hard deadline)
   - X-RW-Flushable: bool ("1"|"0") indicates that partial/approx responses are acceptable and should be emitted early if helpful
   - X-RW-Client-Trace-Id: uuid (propagated for tracing)
   - X-RW-Transport-Estimate-ms: integer (client's measured RTT to edge; used for hedging decisions)

2) Edge/Proxy response headers (edge -> client):
   - X-RW-Flushback-Code: enum ("ok"|"throttled"|"preempted"|"queued") — top-level disposition
   - X-RW-Flushback-Reason: short string, human-friendly code ("capacity_saturated", "kv_miss_heavy", "tenant_quota")
   - X-RW-Served-Priority: echo of chosen priority (may differ from requested)
   - X-RW-Estimated-Delay-ms: integer (approx extra latency induced by queueing)

3) Inflight admission decisions (edge behavior sketch):
   - Maintain per-tenant sliding counters: inflight_high, inflight_interactive, inflight_low
   - Admission rule: allow request if inflight_<priority> < threshold_<priority>. thresholds are tunable per-tenant and function of GPU pool saturation
   - If admit=false && X-RW-Flushable==1: attempt to return early partial response (see partial response strategy below). Otherwise return 429 or queue with backoff hint.

Partial response strategy:
- For flushable requests, runtime will attempt a cheap approximate decode path: e.g., smaller decode depth or shorter sequence limit, or return cached prefix. Response will include X-RW-Flushback-Code: "preempted" and metadata describing what was delivered. Client SDK must display partial text and allow re-request at higher priority.

Client SDK behavior (recommendation):
- Default mapping: typing updates -> interactive; final submit -> critical; background fetches -> prefetch
- If client receives Flushback-Code == "throttled" and it is critical, escalate: set priority to "critical" and retry after jittered backoff (server will log escalation).
- If client receives Flushback-Code == "preempted" with partial result, surface to user inline with an affordance "continue" which reissues a critical request with original context.

Config + rollout knobs (edge operator):
- Per-tenant policy object (YAML-ish):

  priority_thresholds:
    critical: 80
    interactive: 40
    background: 8
    prefetch: 4
  admission_mode: "adaptive" # static | adaptive | capacitated
  preempt_strategy: "shallow-decode" # shallow-decode | cached-prefix | no-preempt
  soft_timeout_multiplier: 1.2
  telemetry_labels: ["priority", "flushable", "admited"]

- Adaptive mode adjusts thresholds based on 1-min GPU busy fraction: threshold = base * (1 - busy_frac)^alpha. alpha tuned per pool.

Telemetry/Observability required fields per request:
- rw.priority (enum)
- rw.flushable (bool)
- rw.admit_result (enum admitted|rejected|preempted|queued)
- rw.estimated_delay_ms (int)
- rw.edge_pool_id (string)
- rw.kv_miss (bool)

Simple ASCII diagram (client -> edge -> serving runtime):

  [client SDK]
      |
      | HTTP POST /v1/generate  + X-RW-* headers
      v
  [edge proxy]
      |- admission check -> counters per tenant
      |- quick path: admitted -> forward to runtime
      |- preempt path: return partial (shallow decode) + mark preempted
      |- reject path: 429 + retry-after hint
      v
  [serving runtime]
      |- fast decode path
      |- shallow decode (for preempt)
      |- telemetry emission -> observability pipeline

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should there be a server-initiated push when a preempted request completes (i.e., notify client via push/WS)? Pros: better UX. Cons: increases server push surface and complexity.
- How to version these headers so older proxies/clients degrade gracefully? Suggestion: add X-RW-API-Version header and default to behavior where unknown values are ignored.
- Partial response format: we need a small JSON envelope that includes: partial_tokens_count, decode_mode, estimated_remaining_tokens. Keep small to save bytes on mobile.
- How to prevent priority escalation abuse? Rate limit number of escalations per client token/session. Track via rw.escalation_count.
- Interop with streaming: streaming currently emits tokens; flushback should map to an early-stream completion event and a trailing header with disposition.

Experiment plan (MVP):
- Phase 0: SDK adds X-RW-Priority & X-RW-Flushable only; edge logs these headers but no action. Collect baseline telemetry for 2 weeks.
- Phase 1: Edge implements admission thresholds and simple preempt path using cached-prefix; roll out to 10% of tenants. Monitor failure modes.
- Phase 2: Add shallow-decode preempt path and client SDK UX affordance for "continue".

Implementation notes for edge engineers:
- Keep admission checks O(1) and lock-free: maintain atomic counters per tenant in shared memory. Use exponential decay sampling for sliding-window approximations.
- Avoid blocking the runtime: if preempt path triggered, spawn a lightweight shallow-decode context with tight token budget and cancel upstream work where possible.
- Ensure telemetry labels are attached early and correlate using X-RW-Client-Trace-Id.

Random scribbles / heuristics I want to remember:
- Map priority -> token-budget multiplier for shallow-decode: critical=1.0, interactive=0.5, background=0.25
- Prefer returning cached-prefix for prefetchs to save runtime cycles
- For mobile: if Transport-Estimate-ms > 200ms and request priority==interactive, edge should prefer shallow decode + prompt to client to retry at higher priority rather than queueing and increasing tail latency

Notes-to-self: sync with UX on how partials are surfaced in mobile message composer. Also talk to telemetry infra about label cardinality and sampling.

End.
